title: Holistic ECG and arrhythmia monitoring with voice biomapping in Berlin
summary: Athletic peak performances, such as running a marathon, place extreme stress on the heart. In medicine, this strain can be measured, among other things, through specific blood markers. However, especially during the recovery phase, cardiac arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation may occur. The actual frequency of such arrhythmias is still unclear. The aim of our study is therefore to monitor athletes during a marathon race and in the subsequent recovery phase using ECG monitoring. We want to investigate how the heart recovers after such extreme exertion. The data obtained from this study will make a significant contribution to enhancing the medical care of physically active individuals in the future.
conditions: Atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter, unspecified

interventions.name: Individuals (n=500) who have independently and voluntarily registered to participate in a marathon will be included in the study. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
None
Exclusion criteria:
Allergy to medical adhesives

Coronary heart disease, history of heart attack or surgical coronary revascularization (bypass surgery)

Cardiomyopathy

History of cardiac arrhythmias or current use of antiarrhythmic drugs

Subjects with (severe) heart valve defects

Subjects after reconstructive surgery (Tetralogy of Fallot, AVSD, hemodynamically relevant defects, etc.)
